purpose: Real result of dispatching .github/workflows/earnings-surprise.yml for the first time, for JBSS's own real filing (CIK 880117, accession 0001193125-25-256406) -- the same case already verified throughout Milestone 3's own work.
finding: SEC's data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyconcept/ endpoint returns HTTP 403 to this exact request (same CIK, same URL construction already verified correct via the built-in browser) from BOTH this Windows machine AND GitHub Actions' own infrastructure -- two separate, real dispatches, seconds apart, both blocked identically. This is a real, structural difference from every other data.sec.gov path this project has used (data.sec.gov/submissions/, used throughout Milestones 1-2, has worked reliably from GitHub Actions every time). Not a code bug: nre.ingestion.xbrl_company_concept() and the CLI command around it behave exactly as designed -- PublicClient.fetch() does not retry a 403 (by design, since 403 is not in its retryable set {429,500,502,503,504}, matching this project's own rule against bypassing bot-detection), and the failure surfaces cleanly as SourceUnavailable rather than crashing or fabricating a result.
what_was_verified_working: The identical XBRL data, at the identical URL, was successfully read through the built-in browser earlier in this same work (both when first designing nre/earnings_surprise.py and when building nre/ingestion.py's own real-data test fixtures) -- so the data itself, and this project's own understanding of its shape, are both confirmed correct. The gap is specifically automated (non-browser) programmatic access to this one API path.
not_attempted: No further retries beyond the two above, and no attempt to alter headers, timing, or request patterns to work around the block -- doing so would risk exactly the bot-detection-evasion this project's own standing rules (and Claude's own safety rules) prohibit. Two consistent, real failures are enough to characterize this as persistent rather than transient.
open_paths_forward_not_yet_evaluated: SEC also publishes bulk 'Financial Statement Data Sets' (quarterly ZIP archives of every company's own XBRL facts, at a different URL under data.sec.gov's own bulk-download page) specifically for programmatic users who need many companies' data -- this may not be subject to the same per-company API path's protection, since it exists precisely to reduce per-request API load. Not yet checked for real.

Reaching out to SEC or waiting to see if this is a temporary tightening of their own bot protection (their own systems change over time, same as the rest of this project has observed for other endpoints).

Restricting real Phase B use to data already reachable through the built-in browser (as was done to design and validate this module in the first place), rather than an automated workflow, at least until one of the above is resolved.
not_a_claim: Not a claim that nre/earnings_surprise.py or nre/ingestion.py's own code is wrong -- both are tested and correct against real, verified data; this is purely an external access-path constraint.

Not a claim that this specific data source is permanently unusable -- only that automated programmatic access to this specific endpoint is currently blocked, unlike SEC's other endpoints this project already relies on.
